title: Sprint-led hire cycler and pricing warp model — Aug 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet explores a timeboxed (sprint-led) hiring cadence coupled with a pricing-sensitivity model we’re calling the "price warp". Goal is to provide a compact operational playbook for 12-week windows where hiring is allowed, reallocated, or paused in response to demand, price movement, and runway constraints.

Summary of mechanism:
- Sprint window: 12 weeks (three 4-week sprints). Each window we allocate a fixed "hire budget pool" (FTE-equivalent) that can be distributed across teams (SRE, Serving Runtime, Sales Ops).
- Hire Cycler: unfilled slots that miss two consecutive sprint windows roll into a "float pool" for reallocation to higher-throughput features.
- Price Warp coefficient (PW): a scalar (0.6–1.4) applied to token-unit price assumptions to stress-test revenue elasticity against unit-cost shocks. PW = spot_price / baseline_price when spot_price available; otherwise manually set for scenario exploration.
- Triggering rules: thresholds for commit/un-commit actions are coverage ratio, rolling 4-week burn vs forecast, and latency of committed deals (signed ARR coverage).

Key knobs and definitions (for model):
- Baseline monthly burn (MB): $3.1M (payroll + cloud + infra reserves)
- Hire slot cost (HS): $18k/month fully-burdened per FTE average (mix of eng, infra ops, product)
- Hire pool per window (HP): baseline 6 FTEs per 12-week window
- Coverage ratio (CR): (Committed ARR expected cover next 12 months) / (run-rate burn) — target CR >= 1.2
- Price Warp (PW): scenario multiplier applied to per-token revenue assumptions to simulate price compression/expansion

Scenarios (12-week window snapshots):
1) Base — PW=1.0, HP=6, MB unchanged
   - Projected 12-week incremental HC spend: 6 * HS * 3 = $324k
   - CR impact: +0.04 (assumes modest deal flow)
2) Price-compression — PW=0.7, HP=3 (conservative), MB +10% due to spot premium for burst capacity
   - Incremental HC spend: 3 * HS * 3 = $162k
   - Net margin delta: ~ -7% on forecasted bookings; runway shortfall ~6 weeks without additional cuts
3) Price-inflation (premium) — PW=1.2, HP=8 (accelerate hiring), MB stable
   - Incremental HC spend: 8 * HS * 3 = $432k
   - Runway improves by ~9 weeks given retained higher take-rates and commit velocity
4) Scarcity shock — PW set to 1.0 but MB +25% (GPU spot shortage) and HP=2 (freeze majority hires)
   - Shadow buffer draw: $780k from reserves required for next 12 weeks

Reallocation policy (operational):
- If CR < 1.0 and PW <= 0.85: immediate hiring freeze; move unfilled slots into float pool; re-prioritize infra/ops hires only.
- If CR between 1.0–1.2 and PW between 0.85–1.05: keep HP at 50% of baseline, accelerate customer success/sales-facing hires to defend retention.
- If CR > 1.3 and PW >= 1.05: ramp HP to 120% for sprint window; authorize up to two expedite contractors.
- Float pool reallocation: quarterly prioritization by Product Finance + SVP Eng; contractors allowed to backfill up to 40% of pool for critical cycles.

Small table (plaintext) — 12-week deltas by scenario:
Scenario | PW | HP (FTE) | 12-week HC spend | MB delta | Runway delta
Base     | 1.0| 6        | $324k            | 0%       | +0
Compress | 0.7| 3        | $162k            | +10%     | -6wks
Premium  | 1.2| 8        | $432k            | 0%       | +9wks
Scarcity | 1.0| 2        | $108k            | +25%     | -? reserves draw

Sensitivity notes and calculations (working):
- PW-to-revenue elasticity: we assume elasticity E = -0.9 for short-term (customers reduce usage when price rises). Example: 20% price increase (PW=1.2) -> expected usage drop ~18% => net revenue change = 1.2 * (1-0.18) = 0.984 (roughly flat) so hiring acceleration is justified if client churn risk mitigated by CS activity.
- Marginal cost per token under different quantization mixes: approximate effective compute delta 0.85x for int8 quant vs fp16. Apply to MB compute line to estimate cloud-savings when pushing customers to quantized variants.

Operational playbook (actions per sprint):
- Week 0 (planning): Finance publishes HP guidance and PW scenario set. Product/Eng submit priority hires + expected impact (throughput tokens/sec or feature MRR).
- Week 2: Hiring committee reviews pipeline; move non-critical hires to float pool if pipeline weak.
- Week 6 (mid-sprint): Reassess CR and PW; if triggers hit, enact freeze or acceleration.
- Week 12 (close): Reconcile spends vs forecast; record lessons and update PW baseline for next window.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: PW underestimates downstream churn if customers avoid high-latency fallback models. Mitigation: instrument per-customer usage and set short-term churn triggers tied to PW > 1.15.
- Risk: Hiring churn costs (offer declines, rescinds) when toggling freeze/accelerate. Mitigation: prefer short-term contractors for volatile roles; keep two prioritized permanent offers per window as a buffer.
- Risk: Over-reliance on float pool creates deprioritization in long-lived projects. Mitigation: product finance gate must re-evaluate before moving >3 slots out of any single team.

Asks for leadership / next steps:
- Approve baseline HP of 6 for next two windows and allow +/-2 flexibility tied to PW triggers.
- Approve contractor budget cap of $180k/window for expedited fill in premium scenario.
- Data work: implement per-route PW telemetry (derive spot_price/baseline_price) and instrument per-customer elasticity proxy by end of Q3 2026 (JIRA-FIN-492).

Appendix — example micro-sensitivity outputs (exportable):
- Export 1 (CSV view): columns = [scenario, PW, HP, monthly_burn_post_hires, runway_weeks, reserve_draw]
- Quick sample row (Base): Base,1.0,6,$3,424,000, 42, $0

Notes (informal):
- This is a working sketch — numbers intentionally coarse to keep the model flexible; finance ops should validate with payroll FY26 actuals and regional comp bands (see linked_confluence CONFLUENCE-8234).
- Slack thread: #finance-hiring-cadence has initial reactions; Omar ran a quick sensitivity showing that moving 2 eng hires to contractors reduces short-term payroll delta by ~35% in first 8 weeks.
